title: midday-jitter-briefing-customer-replay-options-2029-06-07
body:
Audience: customers affected by regional inference jitter (status-page-ready update + customer-facing post-incident summary)

Quick status (for status page):
- Incident window: 2029-06-07 11:42:00 UTC -> 2029-06-07 12:15:00 UTC.
- Impact: transient request latency spikes and response jitter for a subset (~4%) of generation requests routed through eu-west1 and us-central. Briefly increased error rates for streaming sessions (0.7% of sessions) and delayed structured-output completions. No data loss or integrity issues detected.
- Current state: mitigations applied, traffic stabilized, ongoing verification. This is a customer-facing summary + actionable replay options.

Executive summary (plain language):
At ~11:42 UTC we observed an increase in latency variability for inference requests originating in two regions. Some requests experienced dramatic token-level pauses (jitter) and a small number of streaming sessions saw delayed chunks. Our mitigation restored normal service by 12:15 UTC. We are offering an evidence bundle and optional replay assistance for customers who want verification or to regenerate affected outputs.

What went wrong (short technical):
- Trigger: a routing churn event during autoscaling caused a small percentage of live requests to be routed to model-variants that had not yet warmed their KV/attention caches.
- Mechanism: the routing layer temporarily allowed cross-region fallthrough while the local GPU pool performed scaling operations. A race between route pinning and autoscaler updates produced mixed cache states, which manifested as token-generation stalls when a request hit a cold KV cache path.
- Result: latency jitter (pauses ~500ms-2s at token boundaries) and delayed streaming chunks for affected sessions. No model parameter corruption or user data exposure occurred.

Timeline (UTC):
- 11:41:55 — routine autoscaler event begins in eu-west1 (upscale by 2 nodes for a scheduled traffic spike).
- 11:42:12 — small fraction of in-flight requests (est. 3.8%) routed to newly provisioned variants; first jitter alerts fire in telemetry.
- 11:43:05 — alerts threshold breached; on-call paged.
- 11:44:30 — SREs observe anomalous KV-cache miss rates and cross-region route counters.
- 11:46:00 — emergency mitigation 1: disabled cross-region fallback; pinned requests for affected tenants to warm variants.
- 11:50:30 — mitigation 2: increased autoscaler stabilization window to 90s and pre-warmed standby variants in the local pool.
- 12:03:10 — telemetry shows steady decline in jitter; rolling verification begins.
- 12:15:18 — service metrics returned to baseline; incident declared under control.

Immediate mitigations taken (customer-impacting actions):
1) Disabled cross-region fallthrough for the affected routes (temporary) — reduced probability of cold KV path invocation.
2) Forced model-variant warm-up for pinned routes — ensured KV cache primed before accepting live traffic.
3) Increased autoscaler stabilization window and added a short pre-warm phase for future scale-ups.
4) Added token-level telemetry tags to make affected requests easy to search in logs (safe for customer privacy).

Longer-term fixes (what we will do next):
- Routing change: implement stronger route-stability guarantees during autoscale transitions (no cross-region fallthrough until local warm-up complete).
- Cache isolation: ensure model-variant cache namespaces are strictly bounded to tenant/pool to prevent mixed-state effects.
- Observability: add a dedicated alert and dashboard for KV-cache warm-state and route-stability signals.
- Testing: add chaos tests around autoscaler + router interactions to catch regressions.

Customer-facing replay and verification options (how customers can recover or validate outputs):
- Automated replay: we will offer an opt-in replay of affected requests. The replay includes a proof bundle (request id, timestamp, model-version, raw input) and regenerated outputs. Customers can request replay via our incident portal or by filing a support ticket referencing INF-2042.
- Manual replay guidance (self-serve):
  1) Identify impacted requests using the request-id returned by the API or the request_time field (we expose request metadata on the dashboard).
  2) Use the pinned_model parameter in the Redwood API to replay against the exact model-version that was in use (example below).
  3) If you rely on streaming, consider replaying with streaming=false then validating full-output integrity.

API example (snippet customers can copy):
- POST /v1/generate
  headers: { Authorization: Bearer <key>, X-Request-Id: <original-request-id> }
  body: { "model": "rwd-llama-70b-v2", "pinned_model": "rwd-llama-70b-v2@2029-06-07-11-30", "input": "<original-prompt>", "stream": false }

Note: pinned_model uses the stable model artifact tag; our support team can supply the exact tag if not available in your dashboard.

What you can expect from us if you request a replay:
- A proof bundle (request ids, operator timeline snapshot, sanitized logs showing routing and warm-state markers).
- Regenerated outputs delivered in a secure, time-limited link (30 days).
- Optional human review for cases where outputs differ meaningfully and require context.

Customer actions we recommend now (short checklist):
- If you experienced degraded responses, file a support ticket and include one or more request ids.
- Consider enabling pinned_model for production-critical routes during high autoscale activity.
- If you use client-side retries, ensure idempotency_token is present to avoid double-processing on replay.

Verification and evidence you can request:
- Request-level routing trace (shows which region/pool/variant served the request).
- KV-cache warm-state markers for the model-variant at the time of the request.
- Telemetry dump showing token latency distribution for your tenant during the window.

Compensation and SLA: we recognize the impact on production customers. For tenants with measurable business impact we will:
- Offer an account credit proportional to the affected request volume (CS will calculate on a case-by-case basis).
- If you have a Dedicated contract with strict SLAs, our support team will open a formal SLA exception review.

Next communications cadence:
- 2029-06-07 14:00 UTC — consolidated post-incident summary posted to the status page (this document will be adapted).
- Within 72 hours — follow-up with technical RCA and planned remediation timeline.
- We will keep customers who requested replays in a separate notification thread until verification completes.

Who to contact:
- Primary CS contact: maya.chen@redwood.ai (Maya Chen)
- Incident lead (SRE): evan.brooks@redwood.ai (Evan Brooks)
- For urgent partner escalations: partner-ops@redwood.ai

Errors/limitations of this summary:
- This doc is customer-facing and has been simplified; internal operator notes and low-level traces are available on request under NDA for enterprise customers.
- Timing and percentages are estimates derived from telemetry sampling and will be refined in the final RCA.

Appendix — quick search keys for your engineers:
- Request tag to filter in logs: jitter-2029-06-07
- Telemetry dashboard id: infra-routing/Jitter-2029-06-07 (internal)
- Jira: INF-2042

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience. We are treating this with high priority and will provide the verification package and replay assistance to any customer that requests it.
